## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Khaṇikakathā* (Kv 22.8) is a debate found in the twenty-second vagga of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. As one of the earliest textual witnesses to discussions on the doctrine of momentariness, the text defends the Theravādin stance that while mental phenomena are momentary, material phenomena endure for a stretch of time, standing in opposition to rival traditions that posited complete synchronicity and universal momentariness across both physical and mental events [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005]. As Alexander von Rospatt observes, whereas the momentariness of mental states (*Cittatthitikathā*) is addressed in the first half of the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 7.2), the broader question of universal momentariness in the *Khaṇikakathā* appears only near the end of the collection; it was therefore likely incorporated well after the core work was formed, probably by the first century BCE when the canon and early commentaries were fixed in writing [von Rospatt 1995]. Later Theravādin commentarial literature developed this position into the standard theory that material phenomena persist for sixteen or seventeen thought moments [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005].

SuttaCentral registers a thematic connection between the *Khaṇikakathā* and the *Mahāhatthipadopama Sutta* (MN 28) [SuttaCentral]. This link is substantiated by DharmaNexus text-reuse data, which detects eight matching passages between Kv 22.8 and MN 28, notably including near-identical passages at Kv 22.8 §2.8–2.10 and MN 28 §27.1–27.3 [DharmaNexus]. In total, DharmaNexus identifies 207 Pali-internal reuse passages across nineteen texts, with extensive parallels to other *Kathāvatthu* debates—such as the *Puggalakathā* (Kv 1.1), *Sabbamatthītikathā* (Kv 1.6), and *Rūpaṁkammantikathā* (Kv 8.9)—as well as the *Paṭṭhāna* (e.g. *Mahantaraduka*), the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* (*Rūpavibhatti*), and the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also finds automatic cross-language alignments with the Sanskrit *Arthaviniścayasūtra* and Chinese Āgama collections (*Saṃyuktāgama*, T 99, and *Dīrghāgama*, T 1) [DharmaNexus].
